# Adobe Photoshop vs Penpot (2026)

## Overview
Adobe Photoshop and Penpot are two design tools used for creating and editing visual content. This comparison is beneficial for individuals and teams looking to switch from a proprietary design tool to an open-source alternative, with the core use case being graphic design and the key reason for switching being cost and data ownership. The main difference between the two tools is their licensing model and cost structure.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Adobe Photoshop requires a monthly subscription, while Penpot is free and open-source.
* Data Ownership: Adobe Photoshop stores user data on its servers, while Penpot allows users to self-host and maintain control over their data.
* Setup Complexity: Adobe Photoshop has a more straightforward setup process, while Penpot requires more technical expertise to set up and configure.
* Scalability: Adobe Photoshop is designed for large-scale enterprise use, while Penpot is more suited for small to medium-sized teams and individuals.
* Feature Difference: Adobe Photoshop has a more comprehensive set of features, including advanced image editing and manipulation tools, while Penpot has a stronger focus on collaboration and version control.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Adobe Photoshop | Penpot |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $20.99-$54.99/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | MPL 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $20.99-$54.99/month per user | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $20.99-$54.99/month per user | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Adobe Photoshop:**
* Comprehensive set of features for image editing and manipulation
* Wide range of plugins and integrations available
* Industry-standard for graphic design and digital art
* Steep learning curve for beginners
* Expensive, especially for large teams or enterprises
**Penpot:**
* Free and open-source, with a strong focus on collaboration and version control
* Self-hosting option for data ownership and control
* Active community and regular updates
* Limited set of features compared to Adobe Photoshop
* Technical expertise required for setup and configuration

## When to Choose Each
Adobe Photoshop is the better choice for large enterprises or teams that require a comprehensive set of features for graphic design and digital art. It is also the industry standard, making it easier to find talented designers and artists who are familiar with the tool. On the other hand, Penpot is a better choice for small to medium-sized teams or individuals who want a free and open-source design tool with a strong focus on collaboration and version control. It is also a good option for those who want to self-host their design tool and maintain control over their data.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Adobe Photoshop files in PSD or PNG format.
2. Use the Penpot import tool to import your PSD or PNG files into Penpot.
3. Configure your Penpot setup to match your Adobe Photoshop workflow, including setting up your design system and collaborating with your team.
4. Take advantage of Penpot's version control and collaboration features to streamline your design process.
5. Continue to use Penpot for your design needs, and take advantage of its regular updates and active community.

## Our Take
Penpot is not yet production-ready for most users, as it still lacks some of the features and polish of Adobe Photoshop. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Penpot's image editing capabilities are not yet on par with Adobe Photoshop. However, for small to medium-sized teams or individuals who want a free and open-source design tool with a strong focus on collaboration and version control, Penpot is a great option.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams of 1-5 designers who do not need advanced image editing features
* Individuals who want a free and open-source design tool
* Teams who want to self-host their design tool and maintain control over their data
* Designers who prioritize collaboration and version control
* Small businesses who want to save money on design software

## FAQ
### Can I use Penpot for free?
Yes, Penpot is free and open-source, with no costs or fees associated with its use.
### Is Penpot as powerful as Adobe Photoshop?
No, Penpot is not yet as powerful as Adobe Photoshop, but it is still a capable design tool with a strong focus on collaboration and version control.
### Can I import my Adobe Photoshop files into Penpot?
Yes, Penpot has an import tool that allows you to import your Adobe Photoshop files in PSD or PNG format.
### Is Penpot suitable for large enterprises?
Not yet, Penpot is still a relatively new tool and may not have the features and scalability required for large enterprises.
### Can I self-host Penpot?
Yes, Penpot allows you to self-host your design tool, giving you control over your data and workflow.

# Adobe Audition vs Audacity (2026)

## Overview
Adobe Audition and Audacity are two popular digital audio workstation (DAW) tools used for audio editing, recording, and mixing. This comparison benefits audio engineers, podcasters, and musicians who want to choose the best tool for their needs. The core use case for both tools is professional audio editing, and someone would switch from Adobe Audition to Audacity to take advantage of Audacity's free and open-source nature.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Adobe Audition requires a monthly subscription, while Audacity is free.
* Data Ownership: Audacity allows users to retain full ownership of their audio files, whereas Adobe Audition's terms of service may limit ownership.
* Setup Complexity: Adobe Audition has a more complex setup process, while Audacity is relatively straightforward to install and start using.
* Scalability: Adobe Audition is more scalable, supporting larger projects and more advanced features, while Audacity is better suited for smaller projects.
* Feature Difference: Adobe Audition has a more advanced noise reduction feature, while Audacity's noise reduction capabilities are more basic.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Adobe Audition | Audacity |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $20.99-$54.99/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $1049.50-$2749.50/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $4199.80-$10999.80/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Adobe Audition
* Advanced noise reduction and audio restoration features
* Seamless integration with other Adobe Creative Cloud tools
* Multi-track recording and editing capabilities
* Support for a wide range of audio formats
* Regular updates with new features and improvements
### Audacity
* Free and open-source, with no subscription fees
* Cross-platform compatibility, with versions for Windows, Mac, and Linux
* Simple and intuitive interface, easy to use for beginners
* Support for a wide range of audio formats, including WAV, MP3, and AIFF
* Limited advanced features, such as noise reduction and audio restoration

## When to Choose Each
Adobe Audition is the better choice for large teams or enterprises that require advanced audio editing features, seamless integration with other Adobe tools, and robust support. Audacity, on the other hand, is ideal for small teams, individuals, or hobbyists who need a free and easy-to-use audio editing tool for basic editing tasks.

## Migration Path
1. Export your audio files from Adobe Audition in a compatible format, such as WAV or AIFF.
2. Download and install Audacity on your computer.
3. Import your exported audio files into Audacity using the "File" > "Import" > "Audio" menu option.
4. Familiarize yourself with Audacity's interface and features, and start editing your audio files.
5. Take advantage of Audacity's free and open-source nature, and customize the tool to suit your needs.

## Our Take
Audacity is a production-ready tool for most users, offering a wide range of features and capabilities for basic audio editing tasks. However, one specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Audacity's noise reduction features are not as advanced as those found in Adobe Audition. If you're a professional audio engineer or need advanced noise reduction capabilities, Adobe Audition may still be the better choice.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams or individuals who don't need advanced noise reduction features
* Hobbyists or beginners who want a free and easy-to-use audio editing tool
* Teams with limited budgets who can't afford Adobe Audition's subscription fees
* Users who prioritize data ownership and want to retain full control over their audio files
* Small to medium-sized businesses who need a basic audio editing tool for podcasting or voiceovers

## FAQ
### Is Audacity compatible with my operating system?
Audacity is available for Windows, Mac, and Linux, so it's likely compatible with your operating system.
### Can I use Audacity for professional audio editing tasks?
While Audacity is a capable tool, it may not have all the advanced features and capabilities required for professional audio editing tasks.
### Is Audacity free to use for commercial purposes?
Yes, Audacity is free to use for commercial purposes, with no restrictions or limitations.
### Can I import my Adobe Audition projects into Audacity?
Unfortunately, Audacity does not support direct import of Adobe Audition projects, so you'll need to export your files in a compatible format and then import them into Audacity.
### Is Audacity regularly updated with new features and improvements?
Yes, Audacity is actively maintained and updated by its community of developers, with new features and improvements added regularly.

* Setup complexity: StreamYard has a more user-friendly interface and is easier to set up, while OBS Studio requires more technical expertise.
* Scalability: OBS Studio is more scalable due to its self-hosting capabilities, while StreamYard's scalability is limited by its cloud-based infrastructure.
* Feature difference: StreamYard offers built-in support for multistreaming, while OBS Studio requires a plugin to achieve the same functionality.

| Aspect | StreamYard | OBS Studio |
|--------|----------|---------|

| License | Proprietary | GPL 2.0 |

* Offers built-in support for multistreaming
* Provides a user-friendly interface

## Our Take

We recommend switching to OBS Studio if you are a large team or organization that requires full control over your data and needs a high degree of scalability, but not if you are a small team or individual who prioritizes ease of use.

## Who Should Switch
* Large teams (50+ users) who require full control over their data and need a high degree of scalability.
* Organizations that prioritize data security and compliance.
* Technical teams who can handle the complexity of self-hosting and customizing OBS Studio.
* Users who do not need built-in support for multistreaming.

Yes, OBS Studio can be used for multistreaming, but it requires a plugin to achieve the same functionality as StreamYard.

title: Wix vs WordPress.org
comparison_markdown:
# Wix vs WordPress.org

## Overview

Hosted website builder with drag-and-drop interface. is a popular proprietary tool in the productivity space. WordPress.org is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Wix costs Free / $17-$159/month; WordPress.org is Free (self-hosted)
- **License**: Wix is Proprietary; WordPress.org is GPL 2.0
- **Data ownership**: WordPress.org can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: WordPress.org eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: WordPress.org has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Wix | WordPress.org |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $17-$159/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Wix

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### WordPress.org

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [WordPress/WordPress](https://github.com/WordPress/WordPress) * ~19k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Wix if:** Wix is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose WordPress.org if:** WordPress.org is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Wix in its standard export format, review WordPress.org import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

WordPress.org is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Wix tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your WordPress.org instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Wix, switching to self-hosted WordPress.org will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Wix until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Wix paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is WordPress.org free to use?
Yes. WordPress.org is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Wix to WordPress.org?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Wix data, follow the WordPress.org import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does WordPress.org get regular updates?
Yes. WordPress.org has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use WordPress.org without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if WordPress.org development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced June 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Wix](https://wix.com) and [WordPress.org](https://wordpress.org) before making decisions.*
meta_description: WordPress.org is a free, self-hosted alternative to Wix. Compare pricing, features, and migration steps. See full comparison.

# Squarespace vs WordPress.org (2026)

## Overview
Squarespace and WordPress.org are two popular content management systems (CMS) used for building and managing websites. This comparison is beneficial for individuals and businesses looking to switch from one platform to the other, particularly those seeking more control over their data and customization options. The core use case for both tools is website creation and management, with the key reason for switching being the need for greater flexibility and scalability.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Squarespace offers a range of pricing plans, while WordPress.org is free and self-hosted.
* Data Ownership: WordPress.org allows users to have full ownership and control over their data, whereas Squarespace stores data on its servers.
* Setup Complexity: Squarespace is generally easier to set up and use, while WordPress.org requires more technical expertise.
* Scalability: WordPress.org is highly scalable, with the ability to handle large volumes of traffic and data, whereas Squarespace has limitations on storage and bandwidth.
* E-commerce Integration: WordPress.org has a wide range of e-commerce plugins, including WooCommerce, while Squarespace has its own built-in e-commerce features.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Squarespace | WordPress.org |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $16-$52/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | Approximately $26-$52/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | Approximately $104-$208/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Squarespace
* Easy to use and set up
* Built-in e-commerce features
* Good customer support
* Limited customization options
* Data stored on Squarespace servers
### WordPress.org
* Highly customizable and scalable
* Large community of developers and users
* Wide range of plugins and themes available
* Requires technical expertise to set up and use
* Can be vulnerable to security threats if not properly maintained

## When to Choose Each
Squarespace is a good choice for small to medium-sized businesses or individuals who want a easy-to-use website builder with built-in e-commerce features. It is ideal for teams of 1-10 people who need a simple website with minimal customization options. On the other hand, WordPress.org is suitable for larger businesses or organizations that require a high degree of customization and scalability. It is ideal for teams of 10-100 people who need a website with complex features and integrations.

WordPress.org is a good choice for teams who have the technical expertise to set up and maintain a self-hosted website. It is also ideal for teams who require a high degree of control over their data and customization options. In contrast, Squarespace is a good choice for teams who want a simple and easy-to-use website builder with built-in e-commerce features.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Squarespace website data in XML format using the Squarespace export tool.
2. Install the WordPress Importer plugin on your WordPress.org website.
3. Upload the XML file to the WordPress Importer plugin and follow the import process.
4. Configure your WordPress.org website settings and install any necessary plugins and themes.
5. Test your website to ensure that all features and content are working correctly.

## Our Take
WordPress.org is a production-ready platform for most users, offering a high degree of customization and scalability. However, it does require technical expertise to set up and maintain, which can be a limitation for some users. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that WordPress.org can be vulnerable to security threats if not properly maintained, such as keeping plugins and themes up to date.

WordPress.org is a good choice for users who require a high degree of control over their data and customization options. However, for users who want a simple and easy-to-use website builder with built-in e-commerce features, Squarespace may be a better option. Ultimately, the choice between Squarespace and WordPress.org depends on the specific needs and requirements of the user.

In general, we recommend WordPress.org for users who require a high degree of customization and scalability, and Squarespace for users who want a simple and easy-to-use website builder with built-in e-commerce features. Users who are comfortable with technical setup and maintenance and require a high degree of control over their data should choose WordPress.org.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with 1-10 employees who require more customization options and control over their data
* E-commerce websites with 10-100 products that require more advanced features and integrations
* Bloggers with 1,000-10,000 monthly visitors who require more scalability and customization options
* Teams with 10-50 members who require more collaboration and workflow features
* Websites with 100-1,000 pages that require more advanced search and navigation features

## FAQ
### Can I use WordPress.org for free?
Yes, WordPress.org is free and open-source, but you will need to pay for hosting and any premium themes or plugins you want to use.

### Is Squarespace easier to use than WordPress.org?
Yes, Squarespace is generally easier to use and set up than WordPress.org, especially for users who are new to website building.

### Can I migrate my Squarespace website to WordPress.org?
Yes, you can migrate your Squarespace website to WordPress.org using the WordPress Importer plugin and the Squarespace export tool.

### Does WordPress.org have built-in e-commerce features?
No, WordPress.org does not have built-in e-commerce features, but you can use plugins like WooCommerce to add e-commerce functionality to your website.

### Is WordPress.org more secure than Squarespace?
WordPress.org can be more secure than Squarespace if properly maintained, such as keeping plugins and themes up to date, but it can also be more vulnerable to security threats if not properly maintained.

# Adobe Premiere Pro vs Kdenlive (2026)

## Overview
Adobe Premiere Pro and Kdenlive are both video editing software solutions that cater to the needs of videographers, filmmakers, and content creators. This comparison is beneficial for individuals and teams looking to switch from a paid, proprietary solution to a free, open-source alternative, with the core use case being professional video editing. The key reason someone would switch is to reduce costs and gain more control over their data.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Adobe Premiere Pro requires a monthly subscription, while Kdenlive is free to use.
* Data Ownership: Adobe Premiere Pro stores project files in a proprietary format, whereas Kdenlive uses an open format.
* Setup Complexity: Adobe Premiere Pro has a more streamlined setup process, while Kdenlive requires more technical expertise.
* Scalability: Adobe Premiere Pro is designed for large-scale productions, while Kdenlive is better suited for smaller teams and individual creators.
* Feature Difference: Adobe Premiere Pro has a more advanced color grading toolset, while Kdenlive has a more basic implementation.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Adobe Premiere Pro | Kdenlive |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $20.99-$54.99/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $1049.50-$2749.50/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $4199.80-$10999.80/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Adobe Premiere Pro:**
* Advanced color grading tools
* Seamless integration with other Adobe apps
* Industry-standard format support
* Regular updates with new features
* Large community of users and resources
**Kdenlive:**
* Free and open-source
* Highly customizable
* Cross-platform compatibility
* Basic color grading tools
* Limited resources and community support compared to Adobe Premiere Pro

## When to Choose Each
Adobe Premiere Pro is the better choice for large production teams, filmmakers, and videographers who require advanced features, seamless integration with other Adobe apps, and industry-standard format support. Kdenlive, on the other hand, is suitable for small teams, individual creators, and those on a tight budget who need a free, customizable, and cross-platform video editing solution.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Adobe Premiere Pro project as an EDL (Edit Decision List) file.
2. Import the EDL file into Kdenlive using the "Import" tool.
3. Re-link your media files to the corresponding files on your system.
4. Re-apply any effects, transitions, or color grading that were not preserved during the import process.
5. Test and refine your project to ensure everything is working as expected.

## Our Take
Kdenlive is a production-ready solution for most users, offering a wide range of features and customization options. However, one technical limitation worth noting is its limited support for advanced color grading tools, which may be a drawback for professional videographers. For users who do not require advanced color grading and are looking for a free, self-hosted solution, Kdenlive is a clear winner.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams of 1-5 users who do not need advanced color grading tools
* Individual creators on a tight budget
* Teams who require a self-hosted solution for data security and control
* Users who do not need seamless integration with other Adobe apps
* Creators who prioritize customization and community involvement

## FAQ
### Is Kdenlive compatible with Windows, Mac, and Linux?
Yes, Kdenlive is available on all three platforms, making it a versatile solution for teams with different operating systems.
### Can I import Adobe Premiere Pro projects directly into Kdenlive?
No, Kdenlive does not support direct import of Adobe Premiere Pro projects, but you can export your project as an EDL file and import it into Kdenlive.
### Does Kdenlive support 4K video editing?
Yes, Kdenlive supports 4K video editing, as well as other high-resolution formats.
### Is Kdenlive suitable for large-scale productions?
No, Kdenlive is better suited for small teams and individual creators, while Adobe Premiere Pro is more geared towards large-scale productions.
### Can I customize the interface and workflow of Kdenlive?
Yes, Kdenlive offers a high degree of customization, allowing you to tailor the interface and workflow to your specific needs.

# Adobe XD vs Penpot

## Overview

Adobe UI/UX design and prototyping tool. Being phased out in favor of Figma. is a popular proprietary tool in the design space. Penpot is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Adobe XD costs $54.99/month (CC); Penpot is Free
- **License**: Adobe XD is Proprietary; Penpot is MPL 2.0
- **Data ownership**: Penpot can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Penpot eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Penpot has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Adobe XD | Penpot |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $54.99/month (CC) | Free |
| License | Proprietary | MPL 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$2,750/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$10,998/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Adobe XD

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Penpot

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [penpot/penpot](https://github.com/penpot/penpot) * ~33k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Adobe XD if:** Adobe XD is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Penpot if:** Penpot is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Adobe XD in its standard export format, review Penpot import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Penpot is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Adobe XD tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Penpot instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Adobe XD, switching to self-hosted Penpot will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Adobe XD until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Adobe XD paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Penpot free to use?
Yes. Penpot is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Adobe XD to Penpot?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Adobe XD data, follow the Penpot import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Penpot get regular updates?
Yes. Penpot has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Penpot without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Penpot development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced June 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Adobe XD](https://adobe.com/xd) and [Penpot](https://penpot.app) before making decisions.*
